neighbours.label: Actions on machine parts in hands-on mechanical or hardware instructions (yank the manifold, the fan spins, the engine shut down, door unlock): the verb slot of operating or repairing equipment, vs the same instruction syntax in cooking, gardening or everyday text
fire: Loosen the clamp on the radiator hose and pull it off the fitting.
If the starter clicks but the engine won't crank, check the battery cables.
Disconnect the throttle cable, then pry the intake gasket loose.
The cooling fan kicks on once the coolant reaches ninety degrees.
Flip the breaker off before you unscrew the old outlet cover.
The garage door motor hums but the chain does not move.
Tighten the lug nuts in a star pattern, then lower the jack.
When the compressor cycles off, bleed the air from the tank valve.
quiet: Loosen the soil around the tomato plant and pull out the weeds.
If the baby cries but won't eat, check whether she is tired.
Separate the egg whites, then fold the flour gently into the batter.
The choir starts singing once the bride reaches the altar.
Turn the page before you underline the next paragraph.
The old dog sighs but the puppy does not move.
Brush the dough with butter, then sprinkle the sugar on top.
When the meeting ends, collect the papers from the long table.

predictions: Action words in car, appliance and electrical repair sentences reach 0.4-0.75; parallel cooking, gardening and everyday instructions stay under 0.2.
notes: Card: peaks ' blown', 'ank' (yank it out), ' spins' (PSU fan), ' OH' panel, ' banged', ' Smashed', ' shut' (engine shut down), ' unlock'. Probe: yank 0.741, smashed 0.701, fan spins 0.676, door unlock 0.619, 'set it aside on the bench' 0.589 (context, not verb), engine shut down 0.543; 'fan is quiet' 0.268, children ran 0.027, poem 0.016.
